detector._note: Keypoints 23-11-13 / 24-12-14 (hip-shoulder-elbow), 3D world angle. Arms hang at 15-20 and a correct raise turns at 95-105. Past 105 the shoulder stops abducting and starts pressing, which is a different movement and is not counted.

stage._note: Specified by the player, 6 Sep 2026: arms down in the 15-20 band, the raise turns in the 95-105 band, and the arms must come back down for the rep to land. countAt RETURN makes this a whole-cycle rule, so the rep counts on the way down rather than on the way up, which is also the only way the 105 ceiling can mean anything: how far you went is not known until you turn around. plane > 0.5 is the fix for front raises counting as lateral ones. The hip-shoulder-elbow angle is the same 100 degrees whether the arm goes out to the side or straight out in front, so the angle alone cannot tell the two apart; this asks the upper arm to be within 60 degrees of straight out to the side. Measured on traces/reference-lateral-raise.jsonl: at the top of a correct raise the upper arm reads 0.62 to 1.00 sideways (median 0.84), and a front raise reads about 0.

tempo._note: measured window: topExit crossing -> bottomEnter crossing, not the full descent

cues.enter: Face the camera, arms hanging at your sides (15-20 degrees).
cues.tooHigh: Raise the arms out to the sides, not out in front, to about 100 degrees.
cues.framing: I can't see your hips — step back.
